body:
The objection slot was left empty in the first template invocation, so there is no separate criticism to answer; the only critical material in view is the rival's engagement with the account. I note that rather than reconstruct a missing objection. Reading the two supplied texts together, my first judgment is that they are closer than their framing suggests. Much of what the rival criticizes — the quick slide from 'no shared record' to 'make a shared record', the one-to-one approach presented as clearly correct — the account's own commitments had already hedged: it called the record a local trial, flagged the approach as contestable, and proposed treating the whole thing as a test. The disagreement that survives is narrower than it looks. It is this: the account never engages the rival's third reading (the recurring argument as standing-negotiation, the absent record as load-bearing), and neither text says anything about order. That is where I continue.

On the remedy, I use the rival's correction and revise the account's proposal accordingly. The account's concrete vocabulary — task, person, day, what 'done' means — anticipated part of the ambiguity problem, but not recurrence: hearing 'I'll do the dishes' as a standing role versus a one-off offer is a different ambiguity from what counts as done. Taking the two texts together, the operative variable appears to be explicitness at the moment of agreement rather than the medium of the agreement. That a bare written line ('A: dishes, Mon') is no more self-interpreting than the spoken sentence was is the rival's strongest point; and a spoken scope statement that is remembered may be worth more than a vague written one. So I keep the record, but as the carrier of scope and recurrence statements ('this week only', 'standing until the roster changes', what the task covers), not as the remedy in itself.

On sequencing, I revise both texts under a constraint neither names: the household's budget for chore-conversations is plausibly already depleted. One member is avoiding the conversations; a package that adds a standing weekly meeting plus a separate personal conversation spends against that budget before it earns anything. The constraint is a conjecture — the avoidance may have nothing to do with conversation-tolerance — but if it holds, moves should be ordered by discrimination gained per conversation spent: first the rival's one-question probe (three short one-to-ones); then the scope-explicit record, designed to need no standing meeting, with schedule changes posted to it as they occur; a check-in only if the record shows collisions it cannot resolve; and the group-level naming move only if the cheaper moves fail.

On the probe, I use it with the rival's own restrictions and one extension. It classifies disputes — scope, recurrence, timing — rather than adjudicating them; since memory is the contested resource, answers are read for shape, not content. The extension: the rival noted in passing that the probe quietly tests whether the avoiding friend will talk one-to-one. I would make that a planned feature rather than a side effect — ask the friend the same neutral question about past agreements, and do not make their avoidance the topic. Their reception of a content question is the first datum bearing on the mismatch-fatigue conjecture versus the unheard-in-group conjecture, though a refusal would be compatible with many explanations (including being tired of the asker) and should not be over-read. Any conversation whose subject is the friend's withdrawal is deferred indefinitely, on the rival's grounds that a private approach can reproduce the group dynamic at smaller scale — grounds the account's commitments had already half-conceded.

On testing, I revise the account's falsifier because it is too coarse. 'Arguments persist after recording' is compatible with sloppy implementation, with a real but incomplete memory gap, and with the standing reading. Sharper signals, roughly one per reading: if 'what was agreed' disputes fall once scope is stated at the moment of agreement, the scope-ambiguity reading gains; if disputes migrate onto the record itself — contested entries, arguments about who wrote it or who appears on it — the standing reading gains; if the friend re-engages without ever being approached about avoidance, the mismatch-fatigue conjecture gains. One confound I accept rather than solve: if disputes fall, we will not be able to separate recording from scope-stating. Practically it does not matter, since both point at explicitness; for the inquiry it means the first two readings may remain entangled even in success.

What I reject: the group-level naming ('we keep having this conversation; what is it protecting?') as an early move — not as a reading. The ground is that it attributes protective motive to the group before any behavioral evidence exists, and it is the available move most easily heard as accusation; the sequencing makes it unnecessary unless earlier moves fail, at which point accumulated observation gives it something to stand on. What I leave open: the truth of the standing reading, to be tested by watching whether disputes migrate rather than decided now; the load distribution, the chronology of the avoidance relative to the schedule changes, and whether the arguments are escalating — gaps the material still does not fill, and I do not fill them. Last, whether the household wants any of this: the probe doubles as the consent test, and a household that will not answer one question about a past agreement has answered a different question about which remedies are available at all.
commitments: Taking this up involves several separable commitments, none of which is a truth certificate. First, a textual claim that is checkable against the two supplied texts: that the account's commitments had already hedged much of what the rival criticizes, so the live disagreement is the standing reading plus ordering. My synthesis partly rests on that reading; anyone taking this up should verify it against the texts rather than inherit it from me. Second, a claim-type conjecture: explicitness at the moment of agreement, not the recording medium, is the operative variable. It is falsifiable cheaply — if remembered spoken scope statements keep producing 'what was agreed' disputes while equally bare written lines do not, medium matters and I reverse. Third, the conversation-budget constraint is flagged as conjecture, not established fact; low engagement with later moves would be compatible with it and with several alternatives, and should not be read as confirming it. Fourth, the application-type commitment: the ordered trial (probe, then scope-explicit record, then contingent check-in, naming deferred) is a proposed test, not a validated remedy. It depends on all three flatmates being approachable for one question without a mediator, which the avoidance itself puts in question; the probe may return nothing decisive; and whoever runs it commits to not treating non-clustering answers as evidence for whichever reading they already favored — a failure mode the rival named and this continuation inherits. The criticisms carried forward — that the account's falsifier is too coarse, and that the rival's naming move is premature as an opener — come with their grounds attached and are themselves criticizable; in particular, my 'disputes migrate onto the record' signal is not clean evidence for the standing reading, since a badly designed record could provoke contested entries on its own. Scope: this concerns one household's recurring chore disputes; nothing here generalizes to shared housing, couples, or workplaces without new material. Unresolved problems I do not close: the standing reading's status at the outset; the load, chronology, and escalation gaps; the entanglement of the memory-gap and scope readings even under success; and the case where the friend declines even the neutral probe question — there I have no next step that would not be invention, and the honest move is to ask the situation for more material rather than extend the plan. What I currently propose to take up: run the ordered trial, watch the named signals, report observations against each reading rather than fitting them to one, and abandon or revise on the stated triggers.
